question.text: Suppose you have taken a dilute solution of oleic acid in such a way that its concentration becomes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup></math> of oleic acid per <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>cm</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> of the solution. Then you make a thin film of this solution (monomolecular thickness) of area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> by considering <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> spherical drops of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mfenced><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mrow><mn>40</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac></mfenced><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi><mo>.</mo></math> Then the thickness of oleic acid layer will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>14</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. Where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ________ .
